slot.brief: Cleavage of an unsymmetrical/mixed ether with excess HI; show structure figure and ask which alkyl iodide and alcohol form

stem: The ether shown is heated with excess HI. Which pair of products is formed?

verdicts.working: HI cleaves the ether at the propyl–O bond; the aryl–O bond remains intact, forming p-cresol and 1-iodopropane.

working:
$\text{Ar–O–CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI} \rightarrow \text{ArOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}$
Cleavage occurs at the primary alkyl–O bond by $\text{S}_\text{N}2$; the aryl–O bond remains intact.

Independent check: HI cleaves the ether at the propyl–O bond; the aryl–O bond remains intact, forming p-cresol and 1-iodopropane.
solution:
HI cleaves the ether at the primary alkyl–O bond by $S_N2$; the aryl–O bond remains intact.
$$\text{Ar–O–CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI} \rightarrow \text{ArOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}$$
Thus, the products are p-cresol and 1-iodopropane.
